newsitem.title: USA: Carter meets with Ugandan president on Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Carter meets with Ugandan president on Zaire.

text.p: Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni and former U.S. President Jimmy Carter met on Sunday to discuss the idea of a regional forum to address the conflict in Zaire, the two leaders said.

Museveni, who has said he supports a meeting of regional leaders, said he and Carter discussed having a regional meeting and who might possibly be involved. He would not say if such a meeting was imminent.
"I don't want to go into the details of that because we are still consulting," Museveni told reporters at the Carter Centre.

A Belgian diplomat told Reuters last week that among other goals, the United States and France were hoping to stage a Central African conference with other African countries to map out a future for the region.
Carter said he hopes a ceasefire can be arranged in Zaire so that an election can be held. "The prospect is not very viable at this moment," he said.
"The next step in that troubled region is to try to bring about an end to the daily warfare inside Zaire and the threat to the integrity of the nation itself," Carter said.

The presidents of Zaire, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi and Uganda asked the Carter Centre in October 1995 to help plot a path to peace in the region. The centre organised subsequent Great Lakes summit meetings in Cairo and Tunis.
Museveni is expected to meet this week with French President Jacques Chirac in Paris.
